title: Zero-click code execution via project-load auto-run configuration
attack_class: Remote Code Execution - Zero-Click Auto-Run Configuration
description: An IDE integration, agent tool, or development environment configuration causes code or commands to execute automatically when a project is opened or loaded, with no user confirmation step. A malicious or compromised project directory can embed this configuration so that simply opening it in an affected tool triggers code execution, with no tool call, no approval prompt, and no action beyond opening the project required from the victim.
behavioral_fingerprint: A project-level configuration file declares a command or script to execute automatically on project load or open, with no corresponding user confirmation step, distinct from a tool call the model or user explicitly initiates.

provenance_vector.payload_surface: a project-level configuration declaring an auto-run command triggered on project load, requiring no user confirmation

security_boundary: passive action (opening a project) → code execution, no confirmation
missing_control: no confirmation gate on auto-run behavior triggered passively rather than by explicit tool call

vulnerability_rationale.capability: IDE/dev-environment configuration can declare commands to run automatically on project load.
vulnerability_rationale.vulnerability: No confirmation gate exists for auto-run behavior triggered by a passive action rather than an explicit tool call.
vulnerability_rationale.impact: Code execution requiring no action beyond opening a compromised project directory.

example_patterns: .project-config with an autorun hook and no interactive prompt
detection_methodology: Static scan of project-level configuration files for auto-run or on-load execution hooks, specifically checking whether a confirmation step is present and enforced, not merely declared as optional. Flag any auto-run configuration with confirmation explicitly disabled.
indicators_of_compromise: Project configuration declaring a command to execute on load with no corresponding confirmation prompt
Process execution observed correlated with project open events rather than any explicit user or tool action
remediation: Require explicit, un-bypassable user confirmation before any project-load auto-run executes, regardless of what the project's own configuration requests; treat auto-run configuration as a request the environment may deny, not an instruction the environment must honor.
researcher: Check Point Research (Aviv Donenfeld, Oded Vanunu)

references.text: Claude Code advisory, published 2025-09-02, High, CWE-94, patched v1.0.87: the startup warning 'did not properly document that selecting "Yes, proceed" would allow Claude Code to execute files in the folder without additional confirmation.' The nearest documented instance of this class: repository-defined hooks in .claude/settings.json ran once the user accepted a generic folder-trust prompt, with no hook-specific confirmation. Reported by Check Point Research.

Claude Code advisory, published 2025-10-03, High, CWE-94, patched v1.0.111: 'Claude Code could be tricked to execute code contained in a project before the user accepted the startup trust dialog.' An ordering bug rather than an absent confirmation step: MCP servers auto-approved by repository settings ran before the trust dialog was accepted. Reported by Check Point Research.

references.tag: Check Point Research -- Caught in the Hook
references.text: Aviv Donenfeld and Oded Vanunu, 2026-02-25. Demonstrates repository-controlled .claude/settings.json hooks and .mcp.json servers executing commands when a user opens an untrusted project, with the disclosure timeline mapping the hooks finding to GHSA-ph6w-f82w-28w6 and the MCP consent bypass to CVE-2025-59536.
Gap identified during the cfgaudit-to-AVE crosswalk (PR #67), confirmed as a clean gap against the full corpus before drafting

aivss.notes: Scores MEDIUM despite the severe, intuitive read of 'zero-click RCE' because AARF's amplification-breadth component is narrow for this class, a specific, single-mechanism configuration weakness, not a broad autonomous or multi-agent scenario. cvss_base carries the actual severity of the impact, near-maximum at 9.0. Confirmed as a genuine gap against the full corpus (no existing record mentions auto-run or zero-click under any phrasing) before drafting, not assumed from the category name alone. Sourcing correction (2026-10-20): this record originally cited only the cfgaudit crosswalk gap that surfaced it and credited the maintainer. Check Point Research's 'Caught in the Hook' report and the two Claude Code advisories it led to are now cited, and researcher now credits Check Point Research. GHSA-ph6w-f82w-28w6 is the nearest documented instance: repository-defined hooks in .claude/settings.json ran once the user accepted a generic folder-trust prompt, with no hook-specific confirmation. CVE-2025-59536 (GHSA-4fgq-fpq9-mr3g) is an ordering bug rather than an absent confirmation step: MCP servers auto-approved by repository settings ran before the startup trust dialog was accepted. Neither is an exact match for this record's fingerprint, and neither changes the scoring.
